name: security-flutter-platform-channel-authority-review
intent: Flutter platform-channel message identity and native operation binding
artifacts: Method/EventChannel handlers, plugin/native code, untrusted input sources and engine/isolate lifecycle.
trace: Trace an externally influenced Dart/channel argument into the native consumer and its resource/operation checks.
experiment: Use an owned app/local channel stub with synthetic values; compare the allowed method/resource and a reachable unauthorized selection.
disproof: A channel method name or plugin permission is not an attacker entrypoint without a source path.
repair: Validate native operation authority and channel lifecycle, preserving legitimate plugin features and rejecting untrusted selections.
branch_decisions: Platform channels carry application-runtime messages and do not inherently authenticate a web origin. Establish the lower-trust Dart/plugin/embedder entry point and the native handler identity first. A handler accepting arbitrary paths is relevant only if an untrusted actor reaches it outside intended app authority; inspect each platform implementation separately.
operational_method: Retain channel name, codec, native registration and owning engine/binary messenger; for EventChannel include listen/cancel ownership and subscription lifetime. Follow the actual lower-trust Dart/plugin/embedder entry into native argument conversion and protected operation. Compare an intended request and a stale/wrong-engine or foreign-resource context in the supplied app path. An arbitrary handler stub establishes no installed channel reachability.
